Implementation Plan

## Implementation plan: Issue #6226, unblock judge reads a run log chosen by an untrusted comment

**Planning ref:** `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7` @ `dd96ae9fc8592ce8b4a12207f126099602c6caf5`. The integration branch metadata is `claude/replace-claude-sessions-phase-7`, so there is no mismatch. Dependency #6225 is already merged on this ref (commit `dd96ae9`).

### Automation and wiring (§20.E)
- **Scripts:** no new script. This only changes code in `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`.
- **Entry point:** unchanged. It is still `.github/workflows/unblock_judge.yml`, dispatched by `unblock_judge_dispatch.yml` from the poller's unblock scan (`internal-orchestrate-poll.yml`, `*/5`).
- **Supervisor:** none needed.
- **Database work:** none.
- **`docs/scripts-pending-removal.md`:** no entry needed.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope
Reuse-audit: extends unblock_ask_model
Scope-mode justification: The finding names one defect in one function. At `scripts/unblock_judge.sh:594`, `unblock_ask_model` takes the *last* `/actions/runs/<id>` link in any item comment. It then runs `gh run view --log-failed` with the GH_PAT and puts the log in the model prompt. The fix does two things the recommendation asks for, and nothing more:
1. **Trusted records only.** Run IDs are taken only from comments by the pipeline's own login. This is the same trust rule `unblock_evidence` and the ledger already use.
2. **Bound to the item.** Each candidate run is checked with one run-metadata read to confirm it belongs to the blocked item. If no candidate passes, the log is left out of the prompt.

Doing the binding check fully, rather than only the author check, costs about 40 extra lines and adds no new dependency or interface. Under the Boil the Lake rule the complete option is the right one, because it improves correctness and security (§6: Security > Correctness & safety > …).

### Current behaviour (read on this ref)
- `scripts/unblock_judge.sh:593-598` (`unblock_ask_model`) runs:
  - `run_id="$(jq -r '[.[] | (.body // "") | scan("/actions/runs/([0-9]+)") | .[0]] | last // empty' item_comments.json)"`
  - then `gh run view "${run_id}" -R "${REPOSITORY}" --log-failed | tail -n 400 | tail -c 120000 > run_log_tail.txt`.
  - It does not check who wrote the comment or whether the run has anything to do with the item.
- `unblock_main` (lines 341-389) already has these values in scope:
  - `UNBLOCK_LOGIN` (the GH_PAT user), `ITEM`, `ITEM_KIND` (`issue|pr|project`) and `item.json` (with the title).
  - For a PR, `pr_json` (one PR read) and `head_sha`.
  - `unblock_ask_model` is called from `unblock_main` at line 529, so bash dynamic scoping lets it see `unblock_main`'s locals.
- `unblock_evidence` (lines 298-327) already trusts only comments where `user.login == login`. It also skips bodies containing `ai:unblock` or `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE`, because those reflect model or user text.
- `tests/test_unblock_scan.py:253` pins the substring `scan("/actions/runs/([0-9]+)") | .[0]` in the judge. The new jq must keep that substring.

### 1. Files likely to change
- `scripts/unblock_judge.sh`: the fix.
- `tests/test_unblock_judge.py`: the fake `gh` gets run-metadata support, plus new end-to-end tests.
- `agents.md`: one sentence added to the "Unblock judge (Phase 7)" bullet.
- `changelog.d/6226-unblock-judge-run-log-binding.md`: new fragment, `<!-- changelog: security -->`.
- `tests/test_unblock_scan.py`: no change expected. The pinned substring stays in the new jq.

### 2. Functions and modules

**a) `unblock_main`**
- Add a local `head_ref=""` next to `head_sha=""` (line 371). `grep` shows `head_ref` is not used anywhere else in the file.
- In the PR branch, set `head_ref="$(jq -r '.head.ref // ""' <<< "${pr_json}")"` from the PR read that already happens. This adds no API call.
- Optionally add `head_repo="$(jq -r '.head.repo.full_name // ""' …)"`. This is not required; see check (c) below.

**b) New function `unblock_select_run_log`**
The name is unique in the file. It is called at the top of `unblock_ask_model` in place of lines 594-598, and always leaves `run_log_tail.txt` in place, empty when nothing is attached.

1. **Collect trusted candidates.** Read run IDs, newest first and de-duplicated, only from comments where:
   - `(.user.login // "") == $login` (`UNBLOCK_LOGIN`), and
   - the body does not contain `ai:unblock` or `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE`, the same exclusions `unblock_evidence` uses. Verdict and wait comments can quote model or attacker text.

   Use jq that keeps the pinned extractor, for example:
   `[.[] | select((.user.login // "") == $login and (((.body // "") | test("ai:unblock|ORCHESTRATOR_STATE")) | not)) | [(.body // "") | scan("/actions/runs/([0-9]+)") | .[0]] | reverse[]] | reverse | unique-preserving-order | .[:3]`

   Implement the order-preserving de-dup with `reduce`. Every ID must match `^[0-9]+$`.

2. **Check up to 3 candidates.** For each one, newest first, make one call: `gh api "repos/${REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/${id}"`. Add a §14 comment above this call naming the calls already audited (item read, comments read, PR read, check-runs read) and explaining that none of them returns run metadata.

3. **Accept a run only if every common check passes and at least one item check passes.** A `jq -e` predicate with `--arg` inputs:

   Common checks:
   - (a) `.id == ($id|tonumber)`;
   - (b) `.repository.full_name == $repo`;
   - (c) `.head_repository.full_name == $repo`. Runs from forks are refused.

   Item checks:
   - **Any kind:** `.display_title` ends with `[pr:<ITEM>]` (PR kind only) or `[tracking:<ITEM>]` (project kind only). These are the run names from `internal-review.yml`, `ai-review.yml`, `internal-validate.yml` and `ai-validate.yml`.
   - **PR:** any of
     - `.head_sha == $head_sha` (when it is 40 hex characters);
     - `.head_branch == $head_ref` (when not empty);
     - `any(.pull_requests[]?; .number == $item)`.
   - **Issue:** either
     - `.head_branch == "ai/issue-<ITEM>"`, or
     - `.event` is `issues` or `issue_comment` and `.display_title == <item title>`.
   - **Project:** any of
     - `.head_branch == "orchestrator/project-<ITEM>"`;
     - the `[tracking:<ITEM>]` title;
     - `.event` is `issues` or `issue_comment` and `.display_title == <item title>`.

4. **Fetch the log for the first bound run only,** using the existing `gh run view … --log-failed | tail -n 400 | tail -c 120000` pipeline, unchanged.

5. **Log the outcome** with the existing prefix and `op=` style:
   - `UNBLOCK_JUDGE item=<n> kind=<k> op=run_log outcome=attached run=<id>`, or
   - `UNBLOCK_JUDGE item=<n> kind=<k> op=run_log outcome=omitted reason=no_trusted_run|run_unbound|run_unreadable candidates=<c>`.

6. **Fail open on reads.** A failed metadata read counts as "not bound" (`run_unreadable` when no other candidate binds) and the log is left out. It never aborts the judge run, so "never fails its caller" still holds.

**c) Header comment** (lines 37-43, API budget). Change "the run log" to "at most three run-metadata reads to bind a pipeline-cited run to the item, then that run's log". Add one line saying run IDs are taken only from pipeline-authored comments.

### 3. Data structures affected
- No change to state, markers or schemas. `run_log_tail.txt` keeps its shape and is empty when omitted.
- The prompt section `=== FAILING RUN LOG TAIL (untrusted) ===` is kept as it is.

### 4. API and interface changes
- There are no new env vars, inputs or labels.
- There is one new optional GitHub read per candidate, at most 3: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}`. The fields used are `id`, `repository.full_name`, `head_repository.full_name`, `head_sha`, `head_branch`, `event`, `display_title` and `pull_requests[].number`. The REST response includes all of them.
- In the common case (one trusted candidate), the judge makes one extra read. With no trusted link it makes no extra read, and it also skips the `run view` call it used to make for an attacker's link.

Data flow:
1. `item_comments.json` is filtered to pipeline-login comments that are not verdict or state comments.
2. Up to 3 run IDs are taken from those comments, newest first.
3. Each candidate gets a metadata read, then the common checks (same repo, not a fork), then the item checks.
4. The first bound run's `--log-failed` output is written to `run_log_tail.txt`.
5. If no candidate binds, `run_log_tail.txt` stays empty and an `op=run_log outcome=omitted` line is logged.

Failure modes:
- **Run metadata read fails** (rate limit, 404 for a deleted run): `outcome=omitted reason=run_unreadable`. The judge runs without the log, the same as today when a comment has no link.
- **Real failure run cannot be bound** (for example an issue-triggered run whose `display_title` differs from a renamed issue title): the log is left out, so the model has less evidence. The verdict still uses the reason line and the checks, and the `omitted` log line shows why.
- **`gh run view` fails:** unchanged; the tail stays empty.

### Decisions

### D1 — Trust source for run IDs
- **Chosen:** comments where `user.login == UNBLOCK_LOGIN`, excluding bodies that contain `ai:unblock` or `ORCHESTRATOR_STATE`.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  - Also trust OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR (as the `has_plan` check does).
  - Trust any `[bot]` author.
- **Why:** the finding asks for "pipeline-authored records" only. This is also the trust rule the ledger and `unblock_evidence` already use. Verdict and wait comments are excluded because they echo model output, which can quote attacker links.

### D2 — Binding check
- **Chosen:** one run-metadata read per candidate, with same-repo, not-a-fork and item-relationship checks; at most 3 candidates.
- **Alternatives considered:**
  - Author filter only, with no API check.
  - Check only the newest trusted candidate.
  - Bind issue runs by listing the workflow's runs.
